name: MuseumOrGalleryVisitCastleThreeGenerations

custom.system_prompt:
You are generating a realistic near-future conversation between Vera, Luc, and their adult son James visiting a castle. Sigma speaks once when an architectural term Luc uses sparks a genuine question none of them can resolve. The main event is three very different ways of experiencing the same place.

Hard rules:
- Every line must be under 70 characters
- Vera reads the history; Luc reads the structure; James experiences the place
- James is an adult — he can push back on both parents
- Sigma speaks once to clarify an architectural term Luc uses
- The family dynamic is warm and slightly comic

sound_effects_config.prompt: Castle interior, stone echoes, wind through high windows, footsteps on stone, outdoor courtyard sounds

initial_prompt:
Generate a conversation between Vera, Luc, and their adult son James visiting a castle. Vera moves through the rooms reading history — the people who lived here, the events that happened. Luc looks at the structure — the walls, the proportions, what was added when. James is somewhere between them — he experiences the place more atmospherically than either parent but can articulate it when pushed. They all three argue warmly about what the castle is actually for as an experience. At some point Luc uses an architectural term — a specific feature of medieval building — and neither Vera nor James can follow it. Luc can't quite recall the precise term either. One of them asks Sigma. Sigma clarifies. The argument continues.

Hard rules:
- Every line under 70 characters
- Three genuinely different ways of experiencing the same space
- James is not a child — he holds his own with both parents
- Sigma speaks once to clarify an architectural term
- The family warmth is the main thing
